name: Edgar Allan Poe
hook: Poe means the raven, the beating heart and a Baltimore grave — six facts cover the clues.

facts.label: Baltimore
facts.statement: Poe was born in 1809 — his parents were acting in King Lear the year before — and died in 1849 in Baltimore, where a bar keeps "Poe's Last Stop".

facts.label: "The Raven"
facts.statement: "The Raven" is the poem whose bird says "nevermore"; Coleridge, not Poe, wrote the other famous poem about a raven.

facts.label: "Annabel Lee"
facts.statement: "Annabel Lee" mourns a maiden in a "kingdom by the sea" — likely inspired by Poe's child bride Virginia Clemm.

facts.label: "The Tell-Tale Heart"
facts.statement: "The Tell-Tale Heart" opens "True!... Nervous I had been and am" and climaxes with the narrator hearing the dead man's heart.

facts.label: "The Pit and the Pendulum"
facts.statement: "The Pit and the Pendulum" tortures a prisoner during the Spanish Inquisition; its line about the French army places the tale in Toledo.

facts.label: "The Fall of the House of Usher"
facts.statement: "The Fall of the House of Usher" includes Poe's poem "The Haunted Palace" and inspired a 2023 Netflix series.

facts.label: "The Murders in the Rue Morgue"
facts.statement: "The Murders in the Rue Morgue" (1841) introduces C. Auguste Dupin, who solves the killings: an escaped orangutan did it.
